Each new post has a 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD), optional 'slot' (1 or 2, default 1) and 'cities'; the build posts only the one dated today and never reruns old posts (no date = no post). Every post names its own photos: hookImage, slides[].image, endImage. A photo is used once only; 'retired': true marks posts already used. Run 'node src/check.mjs' to catch reused photos and repeated or reworded lines (build.mjs refuses to build otherwise). kind 'list' = slides with title + body; kind 'myths' = myth + truth. 'question' ends the caption to get comments. 'framed': true shows photos whole on cream (history style). Style: all lowercase, no emojis, funny. Dublin voice is irish (grand, deadly, sure look, lads). Health claims say 'linked with', never 'cures'.

stories.hook: how to do a sauna session properly
stories.question: how many rounds do you do?

slides.title: 1. heat
slides.body: 8–15 minutes in the sauna. bail out sooner if you fancy. no medals awarded.

slides.title: 2. cold
slides.body: cold shower, plunge pool or fresh air. even 30 seconds counts. brace yourself.

slides.title: 3. rest
slides.body: sit or lie down for 10–15 minutes and drink some water. frankly, the best bit.

slides.title: 4. repeat
slides.body: two to four rounds is the classic. then finish however your heart desires.

stories.hook: london's secret sauna history
stories.subhook: part 1: steam, scandal and a building you walk past every day
stories.question: what should part 2 cover?
stories.note: pictures: william hogarth (public domain); illustrated london news and st giles bagnio via wellcome collection (cc by 4.0); nevill's postcard (public domain); bishopsgate kiosk by herry lawford (cc by 2.0).

slides.title: london's first steam rooms
slides.body: picture it: the 1600s, no showers, and most londoners rarely had a proper wash. then came the bagnio (say "ban-yo"): a hot room to sweat in, a bath to soak in, and a barber to scrub you, shave you and cup you. this one in st giles was later called queen anne's bath.

slides.title: then it got scandalous
slides.body: soon bagnios were renting rooms by the night, no questions asked, and the word became polite slang for a brothel. william hogarth, the artist who loved painting london behaving badly, set this 1743 scene in one. the husband has just been stabbed by his wife's lover, who is legging it out of the window.

slides.title: turkish bath mania
slides.body: forget gin: the big victorian craze was the turkish bath. room after room, each hotter than the last, then a scrub and a long lie-down somewhere gorgeous, like this cooling room on jermyn street. it was one of the grandest baths in london, until a bomb destroyed it in the second world war.

slides.title: a sweat in the city
slides.body: in 1895 nevill's opened a turkish bath just off bishopsgate, in the heart of the city. bankers and clerks would slip out, sweat off the week, then stretch out in tiled rooms like this one before heading back to their desks.

slides.title: it's still there
slides.body: the baths are long gone, but the entrance survived. tucked into bishopsgate churchyard, two minutes from liverpool street, is a tiny tiled kiosk with an onion dome. thousands of people walk past it every day without knowing what it was. now you do.

stories.caption:
london's secret sauna history, part 1.

1600s: london's first steam baths were called bagnios. you could sweat, bathe and get a shave.

1700s: bagnios also rented rooms by the night, and got a scandalous reputation. the painting is 'the bagnio' by william hogarth (1743), from his series marriage a-la-mode: a husband has just been stabbed by his wife's lover, who is escaping through the window.

1862: the victorians went wild for turkish baths, a row of hotter and hotter rooms. the hammam on jermyn street in st james's was one of the grandest. this is its cooling room, drawn for the illustrated london news. a bomb destroyed it in the second world war.

1895: nevill's turkish baths opened just off bishopsgate, by liverpool street. this postcard shows one of its cooling rooms.

today: the tiled entrance kiosk is still standing in bishopsgate churchyard, two minutes from liverpool street station.

stories.hook: dublin's secret sauna history
stories.subhook: part 1: steam, rebels and a bath from guinness
stories.question: what should part 2 cover?

slides.title: domes beside trinity
slides.body: in 1860 a doctor called richard barter opened dublin's first purpose-built turkish baths on lincoln place, beside trinity college. with its domes and fancy arches it was one of the most striking buildings in town, and james joyce even put it in ulysses. that's it on the left, decades later.

slides.title: a hotel with a sweat
slides.body: on paddy's day 1869 barter opened another one on sackville street, now o'connell street. the hammam hotel had turkish baths out the back, so you could steam, get scrubbed and stay the night, right in the middle of town. notions? fair play to him.

slides.title: a bath from guinness
slides.body: plenty of dubliners had no bathroom at home, so in 1906 the guinness family's iveagh trust opened public baths in the liberties: hot baths and a swimming pool for the neighbours. it closed in 1985, but the red-brick building is still on bride road. it's a gym now.

slides.title: the hammam goes up in smoke
slides.body: in july 1922 the civil war reached o'connell street, and the hammam was right in the middle of the fighting. on 5 july explosions and fire destroyed it. it never reopened, and the hammam buildings stand on the spot today.

slides.title: and then there's the sea
slides.body: dublin never stopped dipping. the forty foot in sandycove was men only until july 1974, when a crowd of women marched down and jumped in. now the coast is lined with sea saunas, so you can sweat and swim like a proper dub.

stories.caption:
dublin's secret sauna history, part 1.

1860: dr richard barter opened dublin's first purpose-built turkish baths on lincoln place, beside trinity college. james joyce even put it in ulysses. the photo is from around 1972, with the old baths' facade on the left.

1869: on st patrick's day barter opened the hammam hotel on sackville street (now o'connell street), a hotel with turkish baths out the back.

1906: the guinness family's iveagh trust opened the iveagh baths on bride road in the liberties, for people with no bathroom at home. it closed in 1985 and the building is a gym today.

1922: the civil war fighting on o'connell street destroyed the hammam on 5 july. it never reopened.

today: the forty foot in sandycove was men only until women 'invaded' it in july 1974. now dublin's coast is full of sea saunas.

slides.title: the ladle merchant
slides.body: one more ladle. and another. it's 110 degrees in here and they're asking if anyone's cold.

slides.title: the silent old man
slides.body: always there first. never says a word. nods at you once and you feel chosen.

slides.title: the gear lad
slides.body: felt sauna hat. personalised water bottle. his own bench towel and a little hourglass. leaves after one round.

slides.title: the one who came for the chats
slides.body: hasn't been near the sauna. been on the bench outside an hour. knows everyone's business.

stories.hook: more types of people at an irish sea sauna
stories.question: tag the wet arse. you know who they are.

slides.title: the revolving door
slides.body: in. out. in again. leaves the door wide open every three minutes and lets all the heat out to sea.

slides.title: the wet arse
slides.body: never brings a towel. sits wherever. leaves a big wet print on the bench like a crime scene.

slides.title: fiadh from foxrock
slides.body: calls it "the spa". asks if the sea is filtered. twenty minutes, then brunch in the range rover. it's 8am.

slides.title: the organic mammy
slides.body: she's 50, glowing, and doesn't believe in 5g. brought her own birch branches and a flask of something green. will outlast you all.

slides.title: the lecturer
slides.body: explains brown fat to anyone within a metre. nobody asked. nobody can leave.

slides.title: the hen party
slides.body: eight of them in matching robes. one is crying, one has lost a shoe. best craic in the building.

stories.hook: even more types of people at an irish sea sauna
stories.question: which one have you sat beside?

slides.title: the clock watcher
slides.body: stares at the clock the whole time. "is that fifteen minutes?" it's been four.

slides.title: the third date
slides.body: both trying very hard to look relaxed. neither can feel their feet. it's going great.

slides.title: the sea purist
slides.body: thinks the sauna is cheating. swims for 40 minutes, comes out blue, calls it "refreshing".

slides.title: the singer
slides.body: starts with a hum. then a full verse. by round three the whole sauna is doing the fields of athenry.

slides.title: the networker
slides.body: handed you a business card in the plunge. wants to circle back after round two.

slides.title: the sleeper
slides.body: lay down on the top bench and was gone. snoring. nobody knows how long they've been there.

stories.hook: signs you need a sauna this week, part 2
stories.question: how many this time?

slides.title: you've been "grand, thanks" all week
slides.body: you are not grand. you're held together by tea and spite.

slides.title: you've cancelled plans twice already
slides.body: the couch has won. one sauna and you'll be human again.

slides.title: your back makes a noise when you stand up
slides.body: you're 32. twenty minutes of heat and it might stop creaking.

slides.title: you've opened the fridge six times looking for nothing
slides.body: you don't want a snack. you want to be warm and quiet.

slides.title: it's been raining since tuesday
slides.body: wet socks, damp coat on the radiator. go and get properly warm.

stories.hook: signs you need a sauna this week, part 3
stories.question: which one is you today?

slides.title: your brain has 47 tabs open
slides.body: nothing switches off. except your phone, which isn't allowed in anyway.

slides.title: four coffees in and you're still wrecked
slides.body: heat, cold, rest. better than a fifth coffee. trust us.

slides.title: you're cold even indoors
slides.body: jumper, blanket, hot water bottle. still freezing. you need the real thing.

slides.title: you snapped at someone over nothing
slides.body: sorry to the barista. go sit in the heat and think about what you did.

slides.title: the weekend went by in a blink
slides.body: give yourself one hour that's just yours. phone in the locker.

stories.hook: signs you should not go to the sauna this week
stories.question: have you ever done one of these?

slides.title: you've had a few pints
slides.body: drink and heat don't mix. it's a real risk. save the sauna for tomorrow.

slides.title: you've just got a new tattoo
slides.body: it needs a couple of weeks to heal. steam will wreck your artist's work.

slides.title: you're full of the flu
slides.body: a fever and a hot room is a bad idea. stay in bed. you're not a hero.

slides.title: you got a spray tan yesterday
slides.body: you'll leave a perfect outline of yourself on the bench. everyone will see it.

slides.title: you've a first date in 20 minutes and your hair is done
slides.body: red face, flat hair, smelling of woodsmoke. actually, that might be a vibe.

stories.hook: signs you should not go to the sauna this week, part 2
stories.question: what would you add?

slides.title: you just ate a massive dinner
slides.body: a full belly in the heat is a rough combo. give it an hour or two.

slides.title: you're running on crisps and no water
slides.body: drink a pint of water first. the sauna will take whatever's left.

slides.title: you think ten minutes in the ice bath makes you hard
slides.body: it doesn't. a minute or two is plenty. you're not a seal.

slides.title: you're only going for the photos
slides.body: the phone stays in the locker. it'd fog up anyway.

slides.title: you've a cold sore and a towel-sharing habit
slides.body: mind yourself and everyone else. bring your own, keep it to yourself.
